    Local contour corrections in Roiter's vanishing argument #

    Package the formal scalar content of the N = 1,2,3 cases in BGRS 8.6. The remaining ray-category work is to produce the paths and balanced arrow selectors required by these lemmas from an efficient tackle.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.contourFunctionClingsToPath_of_related_interlaced {k : Type u} [Field k] {Q : Type v} [Quiver Q] (R : PathContourRelation Q) (I : PathInterlacementRelation R) (c : ↥(contourScalarFunctionSubgroup R)) {x y : Q} (p : Quiver.Path x y) (hone : ∀ (q : Quiver.Path x y), R.related p q → I.interlaced p q) :
    ContourFunctionClingsToPath R I c p

    The path-level N = 1 case: if every related representative is interlaced with p, every contour function clings to the ray selected by p.

      If an arrow-weight family realizes a contour function's ratios from two paths to a common third path, its inverse coboundary makes all three pairwise contours trivial. This is the scalar core of BGRS 8.6(d).

      The paired-arrow correction needed in BGRS 8.6(c). A primary selector occurs once versus zero on the contour, while a companion selector has equal counts; giving both selectors the same weight normalizes the contour.
